data.title: Waymo pauses San Francisco service from Monday amid storm warning
data.description:
• Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Waymo is said to be temporarily pausing ride-hailing services across San Francisco and the Peninsula starting Nov. 23 at 4am PT, ahead of the severe weather forecast for the week.
  • San Francisco officials have been in conversations with Waymo for several days about the forecasted heavy storms and high tides, Mayor Daniel Lurie said in an earlier X post.
  • Lurie has warned that an “extremely serious” situation was about to hit the city, based on National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and National Weather Service forecasts, and urged people to consider not traveling for the holiday.

data.title: Beijing steps up market rescue with record 90B yuan ETF purchases
data.description:
China’s state-backed funds invested a record 90B yuan ($13.5B) in ETFs on Friday, stepping up efforts to support the country’s stock market as a prolonged selloff pushed the benchmark CSI 300 Index into bear-market territory.

The purchases across nine ETFs associated with China’s so-called national team exceeded the previous record of 87 billion yuan set during the April 2025 market downturn triggered by US tariffs, according to Bloomberg.

The Harvest CSI 300 ETF attracted a record 23B yuan in inflows, while the ChinaAMC SSE 50 ETF received an all-time high of 21.7B yuan.

The latest buying comes as Chinese equities face mounting pressure from an artificial intelligence-led technology selloff. The CSI 300 has declined in all but two weeks since August, with state-backed purchases yet to reverse the broader market downturn.

Alongside the ETF purchases, China's three main stock exchanges announced measures to support market liquidity. The Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges will lower the minimum margin financing requirement for investors buying securities with borrowed funds to 80% from 100%, effective November 30. The change, approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, reverses a tightening introduced in January.

The outstanding balance of margin trades fell 1.9% on Friday, marking its steepest decline since July 20, according to the report.

The Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges also announced plans to reduce trading fees, while the Shenzhen Stock Exchange proposed introducing a market-making mechanism on its ChiNext startup board to help curb share-price swings and improve market liquidity.

The record ETF purchases and easing of margin financing requirements underscore Beijing’s efforts to support market liquidity and investor confidence amid persistent selling pressure.

data.title: South Korea's KOSPI drops 5% as AI fears trigger broader stock sell-off
data.description:
South Korean stocks extended their losses on Monday, with the benchmark KOSPI falling as much as 5.41% intraday as investors retreated from technology and semiconductor shares amid concerns over AI valuations, heavy infrastructure spending and potential U.S. export restrictions.

The KOSPI had already dropped 5.21% on Friday. At an intraday level of 4,606.44, the benchmark was down approximately 21.4% from its November 2 close.

Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) fell nearly 6% at one point during Monday's session, while SK hynix (SKHY) also lost around 6%. Over the past month, Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) has declined ~20.1%, while SK hynix (SKHY) has lost around 18.1%, reflecting sustained pressure on South Korea's semiconductor sector.

Among other major companies, Samsung Biologics fell 5.61% on Monday, LG Energy Solution declined 3.26%, Hyundai Motor (HYMLF) dropped 4.90%, Kia (KIMTF) lost 4.42%, KB Financial Group (KB) fell 3.87%, Shinhan Financial Group (SHG) declined 3.94%, and Samsung Life Insurance dropped 4.18%.

The sell-off followed Friday's sharp decline in U.S. technology and semiconductor stocks, as investors questioned the returns on heavy AI infrastructure spending and grew concerned about tighter U.S. semiconductor export restrictions. 

South Korean authorities are preparing a 10T won ($6.8B) stock-market stabilization fund to curb the sell-off and restore investor confidence. The government will also ease restrictions on listed companies’ daily share-buyback orders for three months from November 24, while regulators step up surveillance of illegal short selling and monitor margin loans and potential forced liquidations.

Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said Monday that South Korea's economy could grow in the upper-3% range next year if current trends continue, citing strong exports and investment gradually supporting domestic demand. Consumer inflation is also expected to ease in 2027 as global oil prices stabilize.

However, Lee warned that AI regulation, geopolitical tensions, rising global interest rates, and semiconductor-sector volatility remain key risks. Given South Korea's reliance on chip exports, prolonged weakness in technology demand could weigh on the broader economy.

South Korea-focused ETFs came under significant pressure in November. The Direxion Daily MSCI South Korea Bull 3X ETF (KORU) plunged 54.10% through November 20, while the KICK Korea Semiconductor Index ETF (KCHP) and xETFs Korea AI Semiconductor ETF (KSMH) fell 26.90% and 24.89%, respectively.

Among broad-market funds, the iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) declined 18.70%, while the Franklin FTSE South Korea ETF (FLKR) lost 18.08%. The Matthews Korea Active ETF (MKOR) dropped 18.82%, and the PLUS Korea Manufacturing Core Alliance Index ETF (KMCA) fell 23.07%. The PLUS Korea Defense Industry Index ETF (KDEF) recorded a comparatively smaller decline of 13.51%.

data.title: Australia's Composite PMI falls to lowest level in over five years
data.description:
• Australia’s Flash Composite PMI fell to 46.1 in November from 48.2 in October, marking the second consecutive month of contraction and the steepest decline in private-sector activity since August 2021.
  • Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.7 from 49.6, its lowest since December 2024, while Services PMI declined to 46.2 from 48.5, its steepest contraction since November 2023. Output and new orders across the private sector fell at their fastest pace in over five years.
  • Employment and foreign demand declined, while input and output price inflation eased; business sentiment fell to a three-year low.

data.title: Clariant, CD&R in talks to acquire chemicals firm Ashland - Bloomberg
data.description:
Clariant AG (CLZNF) (CLZNY) and private equity firm CD&R are in discussions to buy chemicals maker Ashland (ASH).

The Swiss specialty chemicals company and the PE firm are negotiating an all-cash deal that values Ashland close to its share price on Friday, according to a Bloomberg report on Sunday, which cited people familiar with the matter. A transaction could come together as soon as the coming days.

No final decision has been made, and talks could fall apart, or another suitor could still emerge, the people told Bloomberg. 

Ashland and Clariant declined to comment. A spokesperson for CD&R didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

A potential deal comes as activist investors have been pushing for months for Ashland (ASH) to explore a sale. In August, Ashland confirmed an agreement with activist investor Ancora Holdings to expand the chemical maker's board.

Last month Dealreporter said that CD&R was partnering with Clariant (CLZNF) for a bid for Ashland (ASH).

data.title: Stock index futures rebound after AI wipeout
data.description:
Stock index futures popped Sunday night, signaling a potential positive open to start the week after the biggest selloff in years.

S&P 500 futures (SPX) rose 0.76% to 6,963.05, while Nasdaq futures (US100:IND) climbed 1.19% to 25,325.85. Dow futures (INDU) advanced 0.61% to 48,442.28.

Last week, the S&P 500 (SP500) fell 8.6%, its biggest weekly drop since the April 2025 tariff crash, and it lost ground on all five trading days. The Dow (DJI) lost 8%, its worst week since the COVID selloff of March 2020. And the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) fell 10%, also its worst week since March 2020.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) (SOXX) fell about 17%, its worst week since the one following the September 11 attacks.

The Nasdaq is in the red for the year, while the S&P and Dow are now in correction territory for the first time since Liberation Day.

data.title: IQVIA nears $1.1B acquisition of UK's Quotient Sciences - Bloomberg
data.description:
IQVIA Holdings Inc. (IQV) is nearing a roughly $1.1 billion takeover of Quotient Sciences.

A deal for the Nottingham, UK-based drug development and manufacturing firm could be announced as soon as Monday, barring any last-minute hiccups, according to a Bloomberg report on Sunday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Quotient is owned by the private equity firm Permira since 2019 and specializes in early-stage drug development. 

IQVIA is set to hold its investor day on Dec. 1.

data.title: Zoom faces mounting estimate cuts ahead of Q3 earnings; outlook in focus
data.description:
Zoom Communications (ZM) is scheduled to report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Monday, November 23, after the market closes. Analysts expect earnings of $1.49 per share on revenue of $1.28B.

Shares fell nearly 15% over the past week, trading 1.19% lower at $82.76 on Friday. The stock initially gained attention following Anthropic's (ANT) record-breaking stock market debut, but those gains faded during regular trading.

Zoom's exposure to the AI startup through its investment stake has added another factor for investors to watch.

The company also recently made a strategic investment in Medaica through Zoom Ventures to support the expansion of its virtual healthcare platform, which uses connected devices and AI-assisted tools for remote medical examinations. In October, Oppenheimer upgraded Zoom to Outperform from Perform, setting a $130 price target.

However, analyst expectations have weakened ahead of the report. Over the past three months, 17 EPS estimates were revised lower, compared with just two upward revisions. All 22 revenue estimate revisions were downward.

Despite this, Zoom has a relatively strong earnings record, beating EPS estimates in seven of the past eight quarters and revenue estimates in six.

Investors will focus on whether enterprise growth and AI adoption can support revenue momentum. In the previous quarter, revenue increased 4.9% Y/Y to $1.28B, while enterprise revenue grew 7.8% to $787.5M.

For the third quarter, management guided to a revenue of $1.275B–$1.280B and adjusted EPS of $1.46–$1.48.

Profitability and full-year guidance will also be important. Zoom previously forecasted FY27 revenue of $5.085B–$5.095B and adjusted EPS of $6.08–$6.12. Investors will also watch for updates on its Anthropic investment and share repurchases.

Seeking Alpha's ratings are mixed: SA analysts and Wall Street rate the stock buy, with scores of 3.83 and 4.13, respectively, while Quant assigns a Hold rating with a score of 3.18. Profitability remains a key strength, carrying an A+ factor grade, while growth is graded F.

data.title: Bears will be yelling fire in crowded theater - Dan Ives
data.description:
The AI trade (AIQ) (ARTY) (THNQ) (BOTZ) (CHAT) faces a bumpy road in the coming months as market fears, political pressure and the departure of Nvidia's (NVDA) Jensen Huang embolden technology bears, but the long-term investment thesis remains intact, according to Yorkville Ives analyst and famed tech bull Dan Ives.

"The bears will feel validated after being doubters of the AI Revolution since early 2023 and will be louder and louder over the coming weeks and months," Ives wrote in a post.

"Yelling fire in a crowded theater moment is here and the bears will take center stage,"amid global market uncertainty and a "Blue Tidal Wave" in Washington targeting Big Tech, creating further volatility for technology stocks, he said.

But Ives argued that the underlying demand for AI infrastructure remains too powerful to derail the broader technology transformation.

He pointed to 160 gigawatts of AI-related power demand and backlog through 2029, compared with roughly 80 GW to 100 GW of planned capacity expansion over the next several years.

"This technology wave will continue at high speed and the Blue Wave, bears, China hawks are not stopping this 4th Industrial Revolution," Ives said.

data.title: 'Hunger Games' helps box office rebound amid GTA 6 fever
data.description:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping brought audiences back to Panem in force, opening with an estimated $120M domestically and helping lift the overall box office sharply from the prior weekend.

Lionsgate’s (LION) latest entry in the franchise debuted at No. 1 from 4,018 locations, averaging about $29,866 per theater. The film added $105M internationally for a $225M worldwide opening and generated $26.4M globally from IMAX (IMAX), the biggest IMAX debut in franchise history.

The broader domestic marketplace collected an estimated $168.08M across 39 reported titles, up 89.5% from the prior weekend but down 8.2% from the comparable 2025 frame, when Wicked: For Good opened to $147M. The top 10 accounted for about $158.31M. Domestic box-office revenue for 2026 now stands at $8.97B, up 20.4% from the comparable period last year and roughly $1.03B short of $10B.

For investors tracking theatrical demand through ticket receipts, the weekend offered a notable rebound ahead of Thanksgiving, even with the launch of Take-Two Interactive’s (TTWO) Grand Theft Auto VI competing for consumers’ entertainment time.

Rentrak’s Paul Dergarabedian said speculation that GTA VI would hurt The Hunger Games appeared misplaced, arguing that “both can do just fine.”

Rocky punches into second

Amazon (AMZN) MGM Studios’ I Play Rocky expanded from limited release into 2,477 theaters and collected an estimated $9.33M, good for second place. Its domestic total reached $10.42M. The film also earned an A+ CinemaScore, a rare mark of strong audience approval.

Paramount’s (SKYD) Ebenezer, last weekend’s No. 1 film, slipped to third with $7.7M, down about 60% in its second weekend. Its domestic total reached $32.5M, with another $45.9M internationally.

Warner Bros.’ (SKYD) The Cat in the Hat placed fourth with $6.9M, followed by Godzilla Minus Zero at $2.7M.

The remainder of the top 10 was tightly packed. You Can See Everything and Wild Horse Nine each collected about $2.5M, followed by Sony’s (SONY) Ghost Soldier at $2.4M, Wildwood at $2.3M and Ramayana at $2.1M.

Thanksgiving next

Studios now turn to the five-day Thanksgiving frame, when several new releases will challenge Sunrise on the Reaping. Disney’s (DIS) Hexed and Universal’s (CMCSA) Focker in Law open wide Wednesday, while Neon expands Paper Tiger and Netflix (NFLX) begins an exclusive IMAX run for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Angel Studios’ Hershey opens Thanksgiving Day.

Last year’s five-day Thanksgiving period generated $290.31M domestically. The record remains $424.9M from 2024, when Moana 2 contributed $225.44M.
